html:
A coastal town east of Abidjan that was the first capital of the French colony of Ivory Coast from 1893.

The French had a trading post there from 1843. As capital it filled with merchant houses, a governor's palace and the customs. A yellow fever epidemic in 1899 killed many Europeans, and the government moved to Bingerville in 1900 and later to Abidjan. In 1949 women marched on Grand-Bassam prison to demand the release of jailed members of Houphouet-Boigny's party, a landmark of the independence movement. Its colonial quarter became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2012. In 2016 gunmen of al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb killed 19 people on its beach.
sum: A coastal town east of Abidjan that was the first capital of the French colony of Ivory Coast from 1893.
